'''Opula Deget''' was a [[Color|golden]]-skinned [[alien]] with brown [[eye]]s<ref name="Visual Encyclopedia" /> who was present outside<ref name="ROTS">{{Film|III}}</ref> the [[Galaxies Opera House]] in the [[Uscru District]] of the [[planet]] [[Coruscant]]<ref name="USW">''[[Ultimate Star Wars, New Edition]]''</ref> in [[19 BBY]]<ref name="Galactic Atlas">''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas: Updated Edition]]'' dates the events of {{Film|III}} to [[19 BBY]].</ref> during a performance of the [[opera]] ''[[Squid Lake]]''.<ref name="USW" /> They walked alongside<ref name="ROTS" /> the [[human]] [[Ulfor Bombaasa]]<ref name="Visual Encyclopedia" /> up the opera house's steps behind<ref name="ROTS" /> [[Duke]] [[Teta (duke)|Teta]]<ref name="Visual Encyclopedia" /> and Duchess [[Koyi Mateil]]<ref name="CVD">''[[Star Wars: The Complete Visual Dictionary, New Edition]]''</ref> when the [[Jedi Knight]] [[Anakin Skywalker]] ran past them on his way to meet with [[Supreme Chancellor]] [[Darth Sidious|Sheev Palpatine]].<ref name="ROTS" /> On the night of the opera, Deget wore a golden [[Clothing|gown]] and a black headpiece.<ref name="Visual Encyclopedia" />

==Behind the scenes==
Opula Deget first appeared in the [[prequel trilogy]] film [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'']],<ref name="ROTS" /> which released on [[May 19]], [[2005]].<ref name="YBY">''[[Star Wars Year By Year: A Visual History, New Edition]]''</ref> The opera steps scene was filmed on R Stage at [[Shepperton Studios]] as part of additional photography on Monday, [[August 23]], [[2004]].<ref name="MakingOf">''[[The Making of Star Wars Revenge of the Sith]]''</ref>

In the new ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[canon]], Deget was first named in the [[2017]] reference book ''[[Star Wars: The Visual Encyclopedia]]''.<ref name="Visual Encyclopedia" /> The character's [[Opula Deget/Legends|name]] originated in the [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] continuity, where it was first used in the reference book ''[[Dressing a Galaxy: The Costumes of Star Wars]]'', which was written by [[Trisha Biggar]]<ref name="Dressing">''[[Dressing a Galaxy: The Costumes of Star Wars]]''</ref> and released on [[October 11]], 2005.<ref name="DressingDate">{{WebCite|url=https://www.waterstones.com/book/dressing-a-galaxy-part-1/trisha-biggar/george-lucas/9780810959644|text=Dressing a Galaxy: Part 1: The Costumes of Star Wars (Hardback)|work=[[Wikipedia:Waterstones|Waterstones]]|archiveurl=https://archive.ph/mxQvt|archivedate=2022-04-24}}</ref>
